open_items.item: Real sync adapter is NOT wired into the shipped app
open_items.detail: main/index.ts constructs an inline stub SyncPort whose acknowledge() returns hardcoded fixtures only when KEEPLING_TEST_SYNC_MODE is set, and null otherwise. The real KeeplingSyncAdapter (main/adapters/sync.ts) is imported by exactly one file: test/e2e/real-stack-sync.spec.ts. So the shipped app never contacts a server. Consequences: nothing reaches PostgreSQL, so the Phase 2 backup infrastructure (infra/backup: pgbackrest, mirror-snapshot.sh, durable-state-manifest.yml) protects an empty database; 'Synced' can never be displayed (D-03 correctly refuses to claim it); and there is NO desktop-local backup or export, so the single SQLite file at ~/Library/Application Support/Keepling/namespace.sqlite3 is the only copy of a user's data. Wiring is NOT a small change: KeeplingSyncAdapter requires baseUrl and accessToken, and the desktop has no server-URL configuration and no sign-in path - DesktopApplication has signOut but no signIn, preload exposes no auth contract, and settings.tsx has no account UI. This is a sixth instance of the GAP-1 class but materially larger than the others. PLANNED 2026-09-02: 03-14 closes this via browser-delegated RFC 8252 authorization (system browser + PKCE S256 + keepling://auth/callback), server-URL configuration, and real KeeplingSyncAdapter construction in bootstrap. Depends on O-18 being closed in the same plan. CLOSED 2026-09-02 by 03-14 (commits f1b505c..b36738b). Verified independently: verify-desktop-phase.mjs lanes=8 failed=0, unit 132->152, ipc 54->66, e2e 53->57, EXIT=0.

open_items.item: CRITICAL - the device-grant OAuth flow is unreachable on any real server (GAP-1 on the server side)
open_items.detail: apps/server config/{config,dev,prod,runtime}.exs never set ':keepling, :device_grants'. The key is supplied ONLY by test setup (apps/server/test/keepling_web/device_grant_controller_test.exs:15, sync_controller_test.exs:14, accounts/device_grant_test.exs:22), which puts issuer/origin/server_instance/redirect_uris via Application.put_env. Consequence on a running server: allowed_redirect?/2 (device_grant.ex:714) reads Application.get_env(:keepling, :device_grants, [])[:redirect_uris], gets %{}, and returns false for every redirect_uri -- so /oauth/authorize always answers 400 invalid_authorization_request; and namespace_config/0, called by issue/3 and exchange/2, returns {:error, :device_grant_configuration_missing}. Three of the five locked namespace-tuple fields (issuer, origin, server_instance) come from this block. Net: no device grant can be issued or exchanged outside the test suite. Same signature as GAP-1 -- a complete, well-tested subsystem that is unreachable in production because its only configuration lives in test setup. OWNED BY 03-14 Task 1, which adds real runtime configuration plus fail-fast pre-supervision validation so an unconfigured server refuses to boot instead of failing later at /oauth/authorize. CLOSED 2026-09-02 by 03-14 Task 1: runtime.exs supplies :device_grants in every environment and Keepling.Application.validate_device_grants!/1 refuses to boot without it. Note infra/compose/compose.yml also required updating or compose boot would have broken.

open_items.item: CLOSED - Quick Entry now returns focus to the prior application
open_items.detail: Found by 03-15 row A9 and documented in 03-15-SUMMARY.md:206, but NOT recorded in HANDOFF.json by the executor -- added here 2026-09-03 by the orchestrator. QuickEntryWindowController calls an optional `foregroundApp` port on open and hide, but NO implementation of that port exists anywhere in the repository and none is passed in main/index.ts#bootstrap(). Prior-app focus return is therefore unreachable in the shipped app. MEASURED, not inferred: with TextEdit focused, submitting a Quick Entry capture leaves Keepling frontmost. Differs from O-1/O-11/O-12/O-15 in that the adapter was never written at all, so closing it is new implementation work (a ForegroundAppPort adapter plus bootstrap wiring) and it carries a real UX decision: what should happen when Quick Entry is invoked from Keepling own window. Disclosed rather than half-fixed. Row A9 fails honestly against it, so the phase gate is RED until it is closed. CLOSED 2026-09-03 by 03-16 (e2bc5ea, 06ac82d, 14a2f4b). `ElectronForegroundApp` in apps/desktop/main/windows/foreground-app.ts is constructed in the production bootstrap() and passed as QuickEntryWindowController's `foregroundApp`. Mechanism: capture records ONLY whether Keepling itself was frontmost; restore calls app.hide(), and macOS hands activation back to the previously active application with the caret untouched -- no TCC Automation prompt, no native module. The UX decision O-21 flagged was resolved as: invoked from Keepling's own window, do NOT hide -- show and focus the main window instead (proven by unit test, since row A9 cannot measure it). The option is now REQUIRED on QuickEntryWindowOptions, so this defect class cannot recur silently. MEASURED: row A9 PASS cases=6 against application_digest=ffcb4a92459956e21708b415f4b4b8b0babde91452ee308a5e633e766d346c59, and the full lane is rows=15 failed=0 cases=92 with LANE_EVIDENCE recorded=true and SETTINGS restore=VERIFIED. The whole desktop phase gate is now lanes=9 failed=0.

open_items.item: Focus return is implemented by hiding the WHOLE application, which also hides Keepling's main window
open_items.detail: Consequence of the mechanism chosen to close O-21, recorded because row A9 does not measure it and a dogfooder will notice it. macOS only hands activation back to the previous application when an application hides ITSELF, so restoring focus necessarily hides Keepling's main window too: capture from TextEdit with a Keepling window visible on the same space, and after the capture commits that window is gone (hidden, not closed) rather than merely behind TextEdit. Every alternative examined needs something we refuse to ship: activating another application by bundle identifier needs its identity, which needs an AppleScript/Automation TCC prompt (prohibited by 03-16) or a native NSRunningApplication module. The next capture un-hides the app again, so nothing is stranded. DECIDE at dogfood: accept it, or ship a native helper. Do NOT 'fix' it by skipping app.hide(), which silently reintroduces O-21 -- row A9 would go red, correctly.

open_items.item: The macOS lane still contains sleep-then-read-once patterns of the class that made A4, A6 and A7 flap
open_items.detail: Three rows have now been caught intermittently failing against UNCHANGED product code: A6 (fixed in fbdf2b4), and A4 and A7 (both fixed in 03-16, b810736 and 1ff88a8). Measured rates before the fixes: A4 failed 3 times in 6 isolated runs, A7 roughly 1 in 8. All three shared one shape -- `await sleep(N)` and then a SINGLE read of AX state that is still moving. Rows A1, A2, A3, A5, A8 and the shared `captureTaskByKeyboard` helper still contain that shape and should be assumed to harbour the same defect until each is either converted to a settle predicate or run enough times to bound its rate. The lane now has a `settledFocus(handle)` helper for the focus case. RULE, restated because it is easy to get wrong: the settle predicate must be strictly WEAKER than the row's assertion (wait for focus to stop moving, never for focus to be on the right element), or the row becomes vacuous. Note also that quiescence is NOT always a valid settle: A7's pending dead key is stable indefinitely, so 'the value stopped changing' would have settled on the failure.

phase_level_gap.ownership_check: Across all twelve plans' files_modified, every plan owning main/index.ts (03-01, 03-10), preload/* (03-01, 03-02, 03-03, 03-05, 03-10) or renderer/* and packages/web-ui/* (03-01, 03-03, 03-04, 03-07, 03-09) is complete. The remaining plans 03-08 and 03-06 are tests, tooling and docs only and touch none of those paths.
phase_level_gap.recommendation: Close O-1, O-11, O-12 and O-15 together in ONE gap-closure plan owning main/index.ts, preload/{contracts,index}.ts and the renderer/web-ui paths. Wiring them separately would re-create the cross-plan file contention that caused this. O-9 proves the class is closable: 03-11 shut it with real evidence against the shipped entry point once a single plan was authorized to own the file. Alternatively record an explicit decision that some are out of v1 scope - but decide rather than letting them pass silently.
phase_level_gap.credential_note: O-15 is the most consequential of the four: an unwired credential adapter means the shipped app's credential path is not the safeStorage-backed one that 03-02 built and tested. Verify what bootstrap() actually uses before any ship claim about credential protection.
